cards.name: route-per-shape-and-rank-backends-under-the-harness-cold-cache-regime
cards.title: Route per shape, and rank the backends under the harness's own cold-cache regime
cards.description: Decode-weighted bf16 GEMM mix: no single backend wins — narrow-N to the in-tree tuned kernel, wide-N/prefill to the vendor library, 1.055x.
cards.key: bf16 a16w16 dense GEMM served as a weighted decode+prefill shape mix on gfx950/MI355X, behind one editable host dispatch file that can pick a backend per shape
cards.effect: 1.055x weighted isolated vs the frozen baseline, whose own arm sat below 1.00x; per-case the narrow-N (N=128) decode bucket goes ~0.66x -> parity, the largest decode bucket ~1.16x, both prefill buckets ~1.21-1.24x, and one decode bucket stays ~0.98x
cards.roofline: every decode bucket sits memory-side of the ridge: the largest one is at ~1.0 of achievable read bandwidth (saturated), the one still open is within ~1.2x of a bare read of its own weights; 40-70% of each decode bucket's timed window is harness graph-replay + event-record infrastructure, which caps the kernel-side ceiling near 1.14x weighted
cards.lever: When a weighted serving mix spans narrow-N decode and wide-N prefill shapes, treat the backend as a per-shape routing decision instead of one global swap: swapping the whole mix to the vendor library scored below 1.00x, while the same library routed only to wide-N and prefill was a win, and narrow-N routed back to the in-tree tuned split-K kernel recovered the rest.
cards.apply: One host-side static table keyed by (M, N, K, dtypes, has_bias) selecting backend plus tuned geometry, behind a warmed launcher cache and a capture guard; keep each contested route switchable by env so a bucket can be re-raced without a rebuild.
cards.stack:
total 1.055x director-verified (weighted) = three lanes hand-merged into ONE route table, not a patch stack
  - 1. narrow-N (N=128) shapes routed back to the in-tree tuned split-K kernel - 1.070x standalone (round 1, verified) - recovers ~23% of the metric and all of the pre-routing loss; the mechanism is kernel quality (~2.2x better at the SAME CTA count), not occupancy
  - 2. the per-shape dispatch table itself, with wide-N and both prefill shapes routed to the vendor library - 1.068x standalone (round 1, verified); the prefill legs are ~1.21-1.24x each, ~10% of the metric
  - 3. the largest decode bucket routed to the vendor library - ~1.16x on that bucket, 1.019x as a standalone lane (round 1, verified)
  - note: attribution is by bucket ownership, not incremental stacking - each lane rewrote the same single editable file end-to-end, so the lanes could not be diff-stacked; a whole second round of backend and geometry search added ~+0.00% weighted on top.
cards.verify: Confirm the intended backend actually engaged per shape (a route trace, not inference from the score), then recompute the weighted score yourself from the per-case line over ALL buckets, median of >=3 interleaved oracle runs; treat a single-bucket move under ~3% as unproven.
cards.pitfall:
printed headline read higher than the honest score -> the harness marks any bucket landing within 1e-4 relative of its baseline as a pseudo-identity and EXCLUDES it, so an unchanged bucket carrying ~22% weight is dropped and lifts the mean -> recompute over all buckets from the per-case line.
an in-process sweep reported a ~24% geometry win the oracle flatly denied -> the first geometry compiled in a process times systematically slow, penalising whichever config is measured first (usually the incumbent) -> compile and time a throwaway config before the real ones.
an autotuner timed with warm back-to-back repeats ranked the vendor library first on narrow-N and scored below 1.00x -> the oracle flushes the last-level cache before every sample -> replicate the flush, one launch per event window, take the median; the ranking inverts under cold timing.
probing several vendor backends inside one process memory-faulted the GPU -> mixed backend initialisation in one address space -> probe one backend per subprocess; the identical candidates were clean that way.
the same build scored ~0.97 under the tracing profiler and 1.055 clean -> profiler perturbation inflates per-kernel medians -> decide by cold-flushed A/B and read the cold minimum rather than any profiled headline.
cards.caution: Also verify a newly registered route wins the cold-flushed autotune before it is taken, so a route swap cannot regress a bucket; and also verify whether your own graph-capture wrapper helps at all here - measured against eager on the same op it was the higher floor, so it can subtract rather than add.
cards.source: run e2e_gpt-oss-120b_20260909_025102 lane, 2026-09-09, gfx950/MI355X; round_1_metrics.json + tech_lead_report.md in the run's eval dir, director-verified
